reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which of these figures has the largest area?

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: 6 squares arranged in two offset rows of 3]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four shapes composed of identical square units are shown:
- Option A: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 3 columns (6 square units in total).
- Option B: A horizontal bar consisting of a single row of 6 square units (6 square units in total).
- Option C: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 4 columns (8 square units in total).
- Option D: A figure consisting of 6 square units arranged in two rows of 3 squares: a top row of 3 adjacent squares, and a bottom row of 3 adjacent squares shifted to the right so that its leftmost square is directly beneath the rightmost square of the top row (6 square units in total).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Cooney has to form figures 1 to 4 with matches.

Figures 1, 2, and 3 are shown below.

He needs four matches to form figure 1, seven matches to form figure 2, and ten matches to form figure 3.

He uses the same rule each time to make the next figure in the pattern.

[Image: that figure 1 forms a square with four matches, figure 2 forms two squares side by side with seven matches, and figure 3 forms three squares side by side with ten matches.]

How many matches will he need to form figure 4?

Answer: ____

descriptors: [Image: four squares side by side formed with 13 matches.]
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
Three figures made of matches arranged in a horizontal row, labeled below with numbers 1, 2, and 3:
- Figure 1: 4 matches arranged to form a single square (one match on each of the four sides).
- Figure 2: 7 matches arranged to form a row of two attached squares side by side, sharing one vertical match in the middle (2 top, 2 bottom, and 3 vertical matches).
- Figure 3: 10 matches arranged to form a row of three attached squares side by side, each adjacent pair sharing a vertical match (3 top, 3 bottom, and 4 vertical matches).

- The shaded polygon has vertices at (3, 1), (5, 1), (6, 2), (5, 3), (5, 4), and (3, 4).
- The left side is a vertical line from (3, 1) down to (3, 4), spanning 3 units.
- The bottom side runs horizontally from (3, 4) to (5, 4), spanning 2 units.
- The right side goes vertically up from (5, 4) to (5, 3), 1 unit.
- From (5, 3), a diagonal side goes up and to the right to grid intersection (6, 2).
- From (6, 2), a diagonal side goes up and to the left to grid intersection (5, 1).
- The top side runs horizontally from (5, 1) left to (3, 1), spanning 2 units.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Three arrangements of 3 tiles labeled Rita, Ina, and Lana]

Rita, Ina, and Lana take turns arranging 3 tiles. Each arranges the tiles in a different shape as shown above. Which of the following is true about the area of the shapes?

options.label: A
options.text: Rita’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: B
options.text: Ina’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: C
options.text: Lana’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: D
options.text: All of the shapes have the same area.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three arrangements of three tiles each, labeled "Rita", "Ina", and "Lana":
- Rita: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. A triangle sits on top of the left square, with its base along the top edge of that square and its apex pointing upward.
- Ina: A square sits at the top with horizontal top and bottom edges. Attached below it is a triangle sharing the square's bottom horizontal edge and pointing downward. Attached to the lower-right edge of the triangle is a second square, tilted diagonally downward and to the right.
- Lana: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. Attached to the right vertical edge of the right square is a triangle pointing to the right.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
